title: fix(pm/fleet-write): re-list a lagging issue list before an issue_create read-back says unfound
body:
Fixes #21181
Clause-②: no

## What changed

The `issue_create` leg of `readBackStroke` in `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` no longer judges `unfound` on its first list. If the repository issue list answers and no issue created since the dispatch carries the title sent, the read-back re-reads that same list on a bounded schedule before it may say `unfound`:

- The schedule is `ISSUE_CREATE_RELIST_DELAYS_MS` = 3 s, 7 s, 15 s: 25 s in all. The self-test holds the sum to at most 30 s.
- It prints one line per re-list, and one line naming the issue and the re-list that found it.

Every re-list is a read:

- ⛔ The create is never re-sent. The self-test asserts exactly one write per stroke, the dispatch, both on a lagging list and on a miss.
- A re-list that cannot be read ends the wait as `unread`, as on the first pass.
- An issue the last re-list still lacks is `unfound`, exit 6: UNCONFIRMED, read the board. Exit 6 means what it meant before. The reason now also says how often and over how long the list was read (`listed 4 times over 25000 ms`).

The `pr_create` and `comment` read-backs are unchanged; the self-test pins `pr_create` as still read once.

## Why: the issue list lags a create (measured)

The table gives each issue's age at the moment its relay run completed, for the five filings in the shift the card reports. The read-back takes its first list within one 5 s run poll of that completion.

| issue | relay run | issue `created_at` | run completed (`updated_at`) | age at completion | read-back |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #21096 | 36824566714 | 06:24:25Z | 06:24:28Z | 3 s | unfound |
| #21114 | 36830404632 (matched by time window) | 07:27:26Z | 07:27:31Z | 5 s | IDENTICAL |
| #21127 | 36835496924 | 08:18:56Z | 08:19:00Z | 4 s | unfound |
| #21135 | 36840884334 (matched by time window) | 09:09:47Z | 09:09:52Z | 5 s | IDENTICAL |
| #21181 | 36873699883 | 14:06:25Z | 14:06:28Z | 3 s | unfound |

Age separates the outcomes exactly: misses at 3–4 s, hits at 5 s, n = 5. That points at list lag, not at the query. `since` filters on `updated_at`, which a brand-new issue always meets, and `sort=created&direction=desc` puts it first. The first re-list, 3 s after the first list, already puts every measured miss past the measured hit age. The 7 s and 15 s re-lists cover a list that lags harder under load. The `found on re-list K, N ms after the first list` line is the reading to retune the constants from.

## Why not the run's own report of the number (route A): probe readings

Triage's first direction was to resolve the created issue from the relay run's report of the number it created. I probed that from this seat container against run 36873699883 (job 110407621005), on 2026-10-02:

| read | answer |
|---|---|
| `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/{id}` and `.../runs/{id}/jobs` | 200 |
| `GET .../actions/jobs/{job}/logs` | 302 to `productionresultssa11.blob.core.windows.net` |
| following that redirect | `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403` (curl exit 56, http 000) |
| `GET .../actions/runs/{id}/logs` | 302 (the same blob storage) |
| `GET .../check-runs/{job}`, `output.summary` | null: the step summary is not exposed there |
| `GET .../check-runs/{job}/annotations` | 200: three rows, two action-input deprecation warnings and one runner-image notice |

The executor prints `#number url` only to the job log and the step summary, and a seat container can read neither, so route A does not exist as the relay stands.

A readable channel does exist: the annotations endpoint answers 200. Using it would mean changing what the relay emits, for example a notice annotation printed by `execute.mjs`. That would be a new report channel: it goes live only once merged, and it costs two more reads per filing. It is named here and not built.

Route B, the bounded re-list, lives entirely inside the read-back. It works as soon as a seat's checkout carries it, and its worst case is bounded. `execute.mjs` and `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml` are untouched.

## Verification (at a5c52b98)

- **Self-test:** `node scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs --self-test` gives `✓ fleet-write/dispatch self-test: 159 cases pass across 16 batteries`. Base `2791138c` gives 146 cases across 15 batteries. The battery floor moves 15 to 16, and the new battery is pinned at 13 cases. It covers:
  - the schedule's shape and its 30 s bound;
  - ⭐ the lagging list (the issue absent until 8 s after the dispatch) reading back IDENTICAL on that issue, exit 0, found on the second re-list at the declared cumulative waits `[0, 3000, 10000]`;
  - one line per re-list;
  - one write;
  - the control: a list that never carries the title is still `unfound`, exit 6, after reads at exactly `[0, 3000, 10000, 25000]`, with one write;
  - a stale same-title issue never taken;
  - an unreadable re-list reading `unread` (HTTP 503 named);
  - a list that already carries the issue read once;
  - `pr_create` still read once.
- **Ablation:** this was run on the committed fix. `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `const relists = isPr ? [] : ISSUE_CREATE_RELIST_DELAYS_MS;` with `const relists = isPr ? [] : [];`. The anchor count went 1 to 0 and the blob `ccea8e06b6c6` to `0abc31df06c2`.
  - Result: red, 7 of 159.
  - The lag fixture returned the card's defect shape exactly: `["unverified","unverified","unfound","objectstack-ai/objectstack (new issue)",6]`.
  - The control, the one-write cases, the read-once case and `pr_create` stayed green.
  - The file was restored to blob `ccea8e06b6c6`, equal to HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- **Gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` derived the same 36 families the dispatch named. All 36 exited 0, and `--ran` reports `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 36 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 36 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero …)`. That includes `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates`, run detached (`dispatch-gates self-test: 1976 cases pass`), and the fleet-write `dispatch` / `execute` / `validate` self-tests.
- **Lint, scoped:**
  - `eslint --no-inline-config --format json scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` returned 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  - The file is in the population: it is not ignored, and the resolved config applies `no-restricted-imports` and `comment-swallow/no-code-inside-block-comment`.
  - Type-aware linting is not enabled (`parserOptions.project` and `projectService` are both null), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The full `pnpm lint` stays CI's.
- **Changeset:** `skip-changeset`, because `scripts/pm/**` publishes nothing.

## Acceptance notes

- The `pr_create` read-back (the pulls list by head) and the `comment` read-back (the comments list since the dispatch) are also list-based, so in principle they can lag the same way. No false negative has been measured on either, so they are unchanged here. This is noted only, not filed. Carrier: none.
- Five readings tuned the schedule. A shift's `found on re-list K` lines are the evidence for moving it. A miss that still reads `unfound` after 25 s, while the issue exists, is the evidence for widening it.
